chapter: Billy Hicks, the Apollo and Roy Eldridge
title: Jam sessions and Roy Eldridge asking him to join
summary: He hunted jam sessions, and Roy Eldridge, whose drummer was leaving for Chick Webb's band, offered him a job at the Arcadia.

bands.name: Billy Hicks and His Sizzling Six

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So, I stayed with Billy Hicks until around the latter part of May, I think it was, and I was in a jam session; you know, because during those days, I mean, every place -- the places to jam were all over, and that's why the unions stopped jamming, because the nightclub operators used to hire like a piano and a drummer, and they'd start at nine o'clock, and nine thirty, you had a whole band up on the stage for free. So that's why the unions stopped jam sessions.

But I used to make every jam -- you know, after I came to New York and found out that I was able to play, even to this day, I am still competitive -- I am very competitive, and I would go out and look for jam sessions, and I would run in to guys like Harold West, Doc West, and Shadow Wilson, and Cozy Cole and Kaiser Marshall. I was competing with these kinds of people in jam sessions. So as fate would have it, I was at a jam session one night, and Roy came in. And they were playing at the Arcadia Ballroom.
Well, the man that was my idol, that I never saw in

person, Chick Webb, passed away. And the drummer that was working with Roy, Bill Beeson, was leaving Roy to take Chick's place at the Savoy. And Roy heard me in this jam session, and he asked me -- he said, "I've heard you before, didn't I?" And I said, "Yeah, that's right, when I first came to town."

He said, "Well, I need a drummer" -- you want to join my band?" Well, I just stood there with my mouth open, because at that time, Roy was at his peak, he was THE trumpet player, and here he is asking me; I hadn't been in New York a year, and he's asking me to join his band?

Well, I was lost for words for a few minutes there, so he says, "Do you want to join my band?" -- and I'm stuttering, trying to give him and answer, and finally, the 'yes' came out. And he said, "Well, you can join the band in July." I forgot what date it was, but I know that it was before the 13th of July, because my first daughter was born while I was playing the Arcadia Ballroom. I called home that night to find out if my wife had had the baby yet, and they told me yes, it was a girl. It was July 13th, 1939.
Well, I had been in the band for about a week before that; in fact, I was married -- when I got married, I wasn't really working regular, I was hitting and missing.
